### L1-607 — `economics.yaml` and `platform-roadmap.yaml` schemas

**PHASE:** L1.6 · **SIZE:** L · **DEPENDS:** L1-101 · **SPEC:** §57.1 (the automation ledger field table); §57.2 (the operating system's own standing entry, "authored in Phase 1, not at Phase G6"); §59.1; §59.2 (the seven investment-gate questions); §59.3 (the change budget block); §50.1 (`control_plane_budget_band`); §52.6 (owners: Founder for economics, Team Lead for the roadmap)
**FILES:** `schemas/registry/economics.v1.schema.json`, `schemas/registry/platform-roadmap.v1.schema.json`, `registries/economics.yaml`, `registries/platform-roadmap.yaml`, `validators/registry/tests/test_economics_roadmap_schemas.py`, `validators/registry/fixtures/econ/**`

**`economics.v1` shape** — `additionalProperties: false`:

```
registry_version : {"const": 1}                                          required
attention_weights   : object (may be {})                                 required
load_model_weights  : object (may be {})                                 required
cost_inputs         : object (may be {})                                 required
control_plane_budget_band : object addlProps false                       required
    currency : string, pattern ^[A-Z]{3}$                                required
    expected : number, minimum 0                                         required
    ceiling  : number, minimum 0                                         required
automation_ledger : array (may be []), items addlProps false             required
    id                                : $ref stableId                    required
    owner                             : $ref stableId                    required
    build_cost_hours                  : number, minimum 0                required
    maintenance_cost_hours_per_quarter: number, minimum 0                required
    failure_cost                      : string minLength 1               required
    human_time_saved : object addlProps false                            required
        before       : string minLength 1                                required
        after        : string minLength 1                                required
        net          : string minLength 1                                required
        source_store : string or null                                    required
    adoption : object addlProps false                                    required
        distinct_invoking_roles : integer minimum 0, or null             required
        source_store            : string or null                         required
    net_value_per_quarter : number or null                               required
    verdict : enum [keep, improve, simplify, retire, unbaselined]        required
operating_system_entry : object or null, addlProps false                 required
    investment_gate_answers : array, minItems 7, maxItems 7, items:      required
        question : integer, minimum 1, maximum 7                         required
        answer   : string minLength 1                                    required
    predicted_saving        : string minLength 1                          required
    scoring_commitment_date : $ref isoDate                                required
    ritual_attention_hours_budget_per_quarter : number, minimum 0         required
```

The `unbaselined` verdict and the `if/then` below implement §57.1's honesty rule: "an entry whose Adoption field cannot name a store is not scored that quarter; it is recorded as unbaselined and the verdict says so." Encode it as `if adoption.source_store is null then verdict must be "unbaselined"`.

`adoption.distinct_invoking_roles` counts **roles**, never people. §57.1: "derived from the event log … never named individuals, because per-person tool-usage tracking is banned outright by Section 91.2." There is no field for a person here and there never will be; L1-803's R-BAN-01 catches any attempt to add one.

`operating_system_entry` is nullable in the schema but §57.2 requires it authored in Phase 1. The nullability exists so the *fixture* corpus can carry a case without it; the shipped `registries/economics.yaml` carries `null` because the seven gate answers are the Founder's (§52.6 owner row), not Lane 1's.

**`platform-roadmap.v1` shape** — `additionalProperties: false`:

```
registry_version : {"const": 1}                                          required
roadmaps : object addlProps false                                        required
    platform : array of string (may be [])                               required
    product  : array of string (may be [])                               required
investment_gates : array (may be []), items addlProps false              required
    initiative_id : $ref stableId                                        required
    answers : array, minItems 7, maxItems 7, items:                      required
        question : integer, minimum 1, maximum 7                         required
        answer   : string minLength 1                                    required
change_budget : object addlProps false                                   required
    period                 : enum [month, quarter]                       required
    max_platform_changes   : integer, minimum 0                          required
    max_fleet_migrations   : integer, minimum 0                          required
    freeze_conditions      : array of string (may be [])                 required
```

`roadmaps` carries the §59.1 split into two lists. `change_budget` transcribes the §59.3 code block, whose shipped values are `period: month`, `max_platform_changes: 4`, `max_fleet_migrations: 1` and the three §59.3 freeze-condition strings — all four are the spec's own literals and therefore transcribable (§0.6).

**NOT IN THIS TASK, and not Lane 1's.** §59.4's process-churn detection, §59.3's tracking of "platform changes per month, migration burden in attention hours, developer disruption hours", and §57.1's quarterly verdict sweep are all subsystem **O**, which PARTITION v1 assigns to no lane. The attention-hour figures they read come from the attention ledger, which is **Lane 4** (`metrics/**`, §99.2 subsystem I). Lane 1 declares the carriers and validates their shape.

**Commands**

### L1-608 — `patterns.yaml` schema and the closed remediation enum

**PHASE:** L1.6 · **SIZE:** M · **DEPENDS:** L1-101 · **SPEC:** §58.2 (the pattern record); §58.3 (the third-occurrence question and the six permitted remediations); §52.6 (owner: Team Lead); AT-040
**FILES:** `schemas/registry/patterns.v1.schema.json`, `registries/patterns.yaml`, `validators/registry/rules/r_pat_01.py`, `validators/registry/tests/test_patterns_schema.py`, `validators/registry/fixtures/patterns/**`

**Schema shape** — top-level object, `additionalProperties: false`:

```
registry_version : {"const": 1}                                          required
patterns : array (may be []), items addlProps false                      required
    id                : string, pattern ^PAT-\d{4}-\d{3}$                required
    root_class        : string minLength 1                               required
    occurrences : array, minItems 1, items addlProps false               required
        record_ref : string minLength 1                                  required
        date       : $ref isoDate                                        required
    remediation_type  : enum [architecture_change, automation,
                              permanent_test, policy_change,
                              product_lifecycle_decision,
                              staffing_decision]                         required
    work_item         : string minLength 1                               required
    closure_condition : string minLength 1                               required
    status            : enum [open, closed]                              required
```

The six `remediation_type` tokens are §58.3's list, closed, and nothing else is admitted. §58.3: **"'Be more careful' is not a permitted remediation."** A closed enum is how that sentence becomes mechanical.

`occurrences` carries `minItems: 1` in the schema, **not** `minItems: 3`. The third-occurrence threshold is enforced by the rule below rather than the schema, so that the error message names AT-040 and §58.3 and so that the invariant register at L1-902 can point at a live check id — the same reasoning L1-201 gives for R-CAP-01.

**Rule `R-PAT-01`.** `SPEC = "Section 58.3"`, `APPLIES_TO = ["patterns"]`. Error when a pattern entry carries fewer than three `occurrences`. Message: `pattern '<id>' records <n> occurrences; Section 58.3 confirms a pattern on the third occurrence`. Pointer `/patterns/<n>/occurrences`.

`registries/patterns.yaml` ships with `patterns: []`. §98.5 Phase G4 populates it and §52.6 makes the Team Lead the owner. Captured content (§0.6).

**NOT IN THIS TASK, and not Lane 1's.** §58.1's pattern **detector** — the thing that notices a third occurrence and raises a candidate — reads incident and postmortem records from `records/**`, which is **Lane 4**'s repository (§52.6), and is scheduled by subsystem **O**, unassigned in PARTITION v1. §58.4's learning-loop chain and SIG-43's postmortem-age sweep are the same. Lane 1 validates the record a detector would write.

§60.2's binding sentence governs the whole phase: **"Simultaneous fleet migration is never required."** Every schema Lane 1 ships must be able to sit beside its predecessor, and the validator must dispatch on the document's own declared version rather than on a global setting. ### L1-701 — Multi-version dispatch: v1 and v2 validated side by side

**PHASE:** L1.7 · **SIZE:** L · **DEPENDS:** L1-309, L1-107 · **SPEC:** §60.2 (the versioned-contract table and the migration flow); AT-025; invariant 73
**FILES:** `validators/registry/versioning.py`, `validators/registry/tests/test_versioning.py`, `validators/registry/fixtures/versioning/**`

`validators/registry/versioning.py` exports:

```python
VERSION_FIELD: dict[str, str]                    # kind -> the field naming its version
def document_version(kind, doc) -> int | str     # reads that field; raises UnknownVersion
def select_schema(kind, doc) -> str              # returns a schema path under schemas/**
def supported_versions(platform_doc, kind) -> list[int]
```

**`VERSION_FIELD` is transcribed from §60.2's table and extended only to the kinds the table's `registry_version` row covers:**

| Kind | Version field | §60.2 row |
|---|---|---|
| `product` | `contract_version` | Product Operating Contract |
| `verification-contract` | `contract_version` | Verification Contract |
| `people` | `registry_version` | People Registry |
| `roles` | `registry_version` | Role Registry |
| `service` | `service_version` | Shared Service Contract |
| `platform` | `platform_version` | Event-type enum |
| `topology` | `registry_version` | (registry, same discipline) |
| `exceptions` | `registry_version` | (registry, same discipline) |
| `policies` | `registry_version` | (registry, same discipline) |
| `os-health` | `registry_version` | (registry, same discipline) |
| `patterns` | `registry_version` | (registry, same discipline) |
| `economics` | `registry_version` | (registry, same discipline) |
| `platform-roadmap` | `registry_version` | (registry, same discipline) |
| `owners` | `registry_version` | (registry, same discipline) |
| `tools` | `registry_version` (optional) | (registry, same discipline; see L1-606) |

The two §60.2 rows Lane 1 does **not** own — `Operational record envelope | records/** | record_schema_version` and `Event envelope | events/** | event_schema_version` — are **Lane 4**'s (`schemas/records/**`, PARTITION lane table). They are absent from `VERSION_FIELD` and `select_schema` raises `UnknownKind` for them. Do not add them; PARTITION rule 4 forbids reaching into another lane's tree.

**Dispatch rules, all mechanical:**

* A document carrying **two** version fields from the table is a usage error (`UnknownVersion`), not a best guess. A `product.yaml` carrying both `contract_version` and `registry_version` is malformed.
* A document carrying **no** version field is a usage error. §60.2: "Every contract schema carries a version."
* A version with no schema file on disk is a usage error naming the missing path.
* `select_schema` **never** falls back to the newest schema. A silent upgrade is the exact failure §60.2's "do not replace" sentence exists to prevent.

**The AT-025 case.** `valid/both_versions_one_run/` holds two product documents in one directory, one at `contract_version: 1` and one at `contract_version: 2`, and both must validate clean in a **single** CLI invocation. `test_at025_both_versions_one_run` asserts exit 0 and the exact line `OK: 2 file(s) validated, 0 error(s)`.

```bash
cp validators/registry/fixtures/product/v1/valid/v1_minimal/product.yaml \
   validators/registry/fixtures/versioning/valid/both_versions_one_run/product-v1.yaml
cp validators/registry/fixtures/product/conformance/valid/service/product.yaml \

cat > validators/registry/fixtures/versioning/valid/both_versions_one_run/expect.yaml <<'YAML'
today: "2026-08-27"
expect_exit: 0
expect_errors: []
YAML
python -m validators.registry.cli --root . --as-of 2026-08-27 --records-root validators/registry/fixtures/versioning/valid/both_versions_one_run --format json
```

### L1-702 — R-VER-01: the supported / transitional / unsupported gate

**PHASE:** L1.7 · **SIZE:** M · **DEPENDS:** L1-701 · **SPEC:** §60.3 (the compatibility state table); §60.2; SIG-09; SIG-10; invariant 74
**FILES:** `validators/registry/rules/r_ver_10.py`, `validators/registry/rules/r_ver_11.py`, `validators/registry/rules/r_ver_12.py`, `validators/registry/rules/r_ver_13.py`, `validators/registry/tests/test_r_ver_10.py`, `validators/registry/fixtures/ver10/**`

**Read this before you write a line.** The master table names this task "R-VER-01 supported / transitional / unsupported gate" and names the file `validators/registry/rules/r_ver_10.py`. The rule id and the module filename **deliberately differ**: the id is `R-VER-01`, the module is `r_ver_10.py`. Nothing in L1-005's four-name contract requires a module filename to match its `RULE_ID` — `discover()` sorts by `RULE_ID`, not by filename. **Do not rename either one to make them match.** Both are named by the frozen master table, and changing either breaks a reference. The three sibling modules do match their ids: `r_ver_11.py` holds `R-VER-11`, `r_ver_12.py` holds `R-VER-12`, `r_ver_13.py` holds `R-VER-13`.

All four carry `SPEC = "Section 60.3"` and `APPLIES_TO = ["product", "platform"]`.

| Id | Module | Condition | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R-VER-01` | `r_ver_10.py` | `platform_compatibility == supported` and `contract_version` not in `platform.yaml → supported_contract_versions.product` | `product '<id>' declares platform_compatibility supported at contract_version <n>, which is not in the supported set <list>; Section 60.3` |
| `R-VER-11` | `r_ver_11.py` | `platform_compatibility == transitional` and `platform_migration` is null, or missing `owner`, `target_contract_version` or `deadline` | `transitional product '<id>' declares no <field>; Section 60.3 and invariant 74` |
| `R-VER-12` | `r_ver_12.py` | `platform_compatibility == transitional` and `platform_migration.deadline < ctx.today` | `transitional product '<id>' is past its migration deadline <d>; Section 60.3, SIG-10, invariant 74` |
| `R-VER-13` | `r_ver_13.py` | `platform_compatibility == unsupported` | `product '<id>' is unsupported; Section 60.3 blocks deployment until it migrates` |

§60.3's table gives each state its consequence in terms: `transitional` "**Requires a named migration owner, a target version and a deadline**"; `unsupported` means "**Deployment blocked.** Escalates automatically". R-VER-13 fires on the declaration alone, because the declaration *is* the blocked state.

R-VER-01 and R-VER-11/12/13 return **zero errors** when `platform.yaml` is absent from `ctx.docs` (R-VER-01) or when `product.yaml` is (all four). R-VER-12's boundary is strict `<`: a deadline falling **today** is not yet past. `valid/transitional_deadline_today/` proves it.

### L1-704 — R-INV-01: the 29-artifact inventory guard

**PHASE:** L1.7 · **SIZE:** M · **DEPENDS:** L1-505 · **SPEC:** §52.6 ("This table is the complete inventory — twenty-nine entries. Any proposal for a new control-plane artifact must state which existing file cannot hold the content"); §0.7
**FILES:** `validators/registry/rules/r_inv_01.py`, `validators/registry/rules/r_inv_03.py`, `registries/INVENTORY.yaml`, `validators/registry/tests/test_r_inv_01.py`, `validators/registry/fixtures/inv/**`

**`registries/INVENTORY.yaml` holds no artifact list.** The list lives in `registries/OWNERS.yaml` (L1-505) and duplicating it would be a second copy of a shared list — precisely what PARTITION rule 3 forbids and what §52.2's "the table is a view of it, never a second copy" discipline warns against. `INVENTORY.yaml` holds the **declared count and the exemption list** only:

```
registry_version : {"const": 1}                                          required
source           : string minLength 1                                    required
owners_manifest  : string minLength 1                                    required
tooling_exempt   : array of string (may be [])                           required
```

`tooling_exempt` lists path globs under `registries/**` that §0.7 exempts because they describe the inventory rather than hold control-plane content. It ships holding exactly the three files that provoked the L1-505 blocker.

**Rules:**

| Id | Module | Condition | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R-INV-01` | `r_inv_01.py` | `len(owners.artifacts)` differs from `owners.declared_count` | `the owner manifest lists <n> control-plane artifacts; declared_count is <m>; Section 52.6` |
| `R-INV-03` | `r_inv_03.py` | a file under `registries/` matching no `owners.artifacts[].path` and no `tooling_exempt` glob | `registries/<f> is a control-plane artifact absent from the owner manifest; Section 52.6 requires a new artifact to state which existing file cannot hold it` |

`R-INV-02` is **not** allocated here. It belongs to L1-902's invariant-classification rule; leave the id free.

Both rules return **zero errors** when `owners` is absent from `ctx.docs`.

**KNOWN RED — expected, and correct.** `registries/OWNERS.yaml` ships with thirty artifacts and `declared_count: 29`, because §52.6 states twenty-nine and renders thirty (see the L1-505 blocker). R-INV-01 therefore fires on the live tree, and `INVENTORY_LIVE_EXIT=1` is the **correct** result until L0 answers. This is the same arrangement L1-202 uses for the `founder` role row. Record it in the PR body as `known-red, blocked on L1-505`. **Do not edit `OWNERS.yaml` to make it green** — that would launder the discrepancy the guard exists to surface.

### L1-705 — Schema-change checklist generator

**PHASE:** L1.7 · **SIZE:** M · **DEPENDS:** L1-703 · **SPEC:** §60.2 (the migration flow diagram, nine steps); AT-025; invariant 73
**FILES:** `validators/registry/tools/schema_change.py`, `validators/registry/tests/test_schema_change_tool.py`

§60.2's migration flow is nine ordered steps and every schema change in this system must walk them. The tool turns that flow into a checklist so no step is skipped from memory.

**Invocation:**

```
python -m validators.registry.tools.schema_change --kind <kind> --from <n> --to <n>
```

**Exit codes**, matching the frozen grammar of L1-003:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | checklist emitted |
| 2 | usage error — unknown `--kind`, `--to` is not `--from + 1`, either value is not a positive integer |

**The nine steps, verbatim in this order** from the §60.2 flow diagram:

1. Schema change proposed
2. Write the v`<to>` schema alongside v`<from>` — do not replace
3. Validator supports BOTH v`<from>` and v`<to>`
4. Write the migration — automated where possible
5. Canary products migrate first
6. Verify
7. Fleet migrates gradually, each product on its own schedule
8. v`<from>` deprecation deadline set and published
9. v`<from>` support removed only after every product has migrated

**The tool writes nothing.** It emits the checklist on stdout and exits. It never creates, edits or deletes a schema file. `test_writes_no_files` snapshots the tree before and after and asserts they are identical — a generator that silently scaffolds a schema is how step 2's "do not replace" gets skipped.

`--kind` accepts exactly the keys of `versioning.VERSION_FIELD` (L1-701) and nothing else. `test_kind_list_matches_versioning_table` asserts the two sets are equal, so a kind added to one is never missing from the other.

**Commands**

```bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$REPO_ROOT"
git fetch origin
git status --porcelain
git checkout -B lane/1/l1-705 origin/integration
mkdir -p validators/registry/tools
```

Then author `validators/registry/tools/schema_change.py` and `validators/registry/tests/test_schema_change_tool.py` with exactly these seven test functions:

| Test | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `test_emits_nine_steps` | stdout holds exactly nine numbered lines |
| `test_step_order_matches_spec` | the nine lines appear in the §60.2 order, with `alongside` in step 2 and `BOTH` in step 3 |
| `test_writes_no_files` | the working tree is byte-identical before and after |
| `test_unknown_kind_is_exit_2` | `--kind records` exits 2 |
| `test_non_adjacent_version_is_exit_2` | `--from 1 --to 3` exits 2 |
| `test_downgrade_is_exit_2` | `--from 2 --to 1` exits 2 |
| `test_kind_list_matches_versioning_table` | the tool's accepted kinds equal `set(versioning.VERSION_FIELD)` |

## PHASE L1.8 — THE PEOPLE LAYER BOUNDARY

Spec anchor: §98.6 **Phase P2 — Registries and framework mapping**; §77 (Performance Framework Registry); §91.2 (no-surveillance design); §90.4 (the people-intelligence capability, not delegable); §74.5 (the authority matrix); invariants 37, 96–99, 106.

**DEPENDENCY ON AN UNASSIGNED SUBSYSTEM — state it, route it, do not claim it.** §99.2 subsystem **P** ("People intelligence engine") holds capacity profiles, utilisation composition, overload detection, evidence bundles, succession and dependency risk. **PARTITION v1 assigns subsystem P to no lane**, and §99.2's dependency spine adds "P is hard-gated on L's datasource separation" — subsystem **L**, which PARTITION v1 gives to Lane 5 (`access/**`). Lane 1 builds the **framework registry schema** and the **denial rules**, both of which live in Lane 1 paths. Lane 1 builds no evidence bundle, no capacity profile, no per-person anything.

**The boundary this phase enforces, stated once and binding on every task in it.** §91.2 bans eleven measurement classes outright, "with no configuration option to enable any of them". Invariant 37 forbids any automated formal people action. §90.4 makes `people-intelligence` non-delegable (D109). Lane 1's job here is to make each of those **mechanically impossible to configure**, which is exactly what AT-071, AT-075 and AT-090 test. Lane 1 never holds, reads or models an individual's performance data — that is Layer B, whose durable home §52.6 puts outside every org-readable repository.

**§78 is a snapshot, not a source.** §0.6 and §99.6 both say so, and §78.1 says it of itself. **Never transcribe a §78 KRA, KPI, weight, target or roster row into `registries/framework/**`.** Framework content is captured by the Founder under the §77.4 change authority. Roster-shaped test data uses the spec's own placeholder ids only.

### L1-801 — Performance framework registry schema

**PHASE:** L1.8 · **SIZE:** L · **DEPENDS:** L1-102 · **SPEC:** §77.1 (the registry field table); §77.2 (variable structure per role); §77.4 (the `Not defined in Framework v1` literal); §84.6 (`time_window` and `known_limitations` required on every framework KPI); §52.6 (Performance framework registry, owner: Founder); AT-014
**FILES:** `schemas/registry/framework.v1.schema.json`, `registries/framework/.gitkeep`, `validators/registry/tests/test_framework_schema.py`, `validators/registry/fixtures/framework/**`

**Directory-per-item.** One file per framework version, `registries/framework/<framework_version>.yaml`. PARTITION rule 3 forbids a single file listing every version, and §77.1's "Retirement date | Set when superseded; never deleted" means versions accumulate — exactly the shape that would turn a single file into a shared mutable index. §52.6 counts the "Performance framework registry" as **one** inventory entry, so the tree creates no thirtieth artifact (§0.7).

**Schema shape** — top-level object, `additionalProperties: false`, transcribed from §77.1's field table:

```
framework_version : string, pattern ^v\d+(\.\d+)?$                       required
status            : enum [draft, pilot, active, deprecated, retired]     required
effective_date    : $ref isoDate                                         required
retirement_date   : $ref isoDateOrNull                                   required
affected_roles    : array of $ref stableId, minItems 1, unique           required
multi_framework_transition : boolean                                     optional
review_cadence    : string minLength 1                                   required
rating_scale : object addlProps false                                    required
    verbatim : {"const": true}                                           required
    bands    : array, minItems 1, items addlProps false                  required
        label      : string minLength 1                                  required
        definition : string minLength 1                                  required
kras : array (may be []), items addlProps false                          required
    id         : string minLength 1                                      required
    title      : string minLength 1                                      required
    weight     : number, minimum 0, maximum 100                          required
    definition : string minLength 1                                      required
kpis : array (may be []), items addlProps false                          required
    id                    : string minLength 1                           required
    kra_id                : string or null                               required
    title                 : string minLength 1                           required
    weight                : number, minimum 0, maximum 100               required
    definition            : string minLength 1                           required
    target                : string minLength 1                           required
    stretch_target        : string or null                               required
    evidence_sources      : array of string (may be [])                  required
    human_judgement_areas : array of string (may be [])                  required
    time_window           : string minLength 1                           required
    known_limitations     : string minLength 1                           required
```

**`kras` and `kpis` carry no `minItems` and no maximum.** §77.2 is explicit: "The number of KRAs and KPIs is configuration, not architecture. The registry must support a role with three KPIs, a role with six, a role with ten, and a role with an entirely custom evaluation structure that does not use KRA/KPI vocabulary at all." A count constraint here would break AT-014.

**`kpis[].kra_id` is nullable** for the same reason: a framework that does not use KRA vocabulary carries KPIs that hang off nothing.

**`rating_scale.verbatim` is `{"const": true}`.** §77.1: "The framework's own rating bands, recorded verbatim; the registry imposes none of its own." A registry that could record a non-verbatim scale would be imposing one.

**`time_window` and `known_limitations` are required on every KPI.** §84.6: "`time_window` and `known_limitations` are required fields wherever the metric is registered … on every framework KPI in the evidence-mapping register of Section 79." Both are `minLength 1`; where a limitation is genuinely absent the value is the literal `none-known` (§84.6).

**`review_cadence` may hold the literal `Not defined`.** §77.1: "where the framework in force defines none, the field records exactly `Not defined` and the Founder sets an operational cadence at registry activation." Note that this literal — `Not defined` — is **different** from §77.4's field-level marker `Not defined in Framework v1`. Both are load-bearing and neither substitutes for the other. L1-802's `R-FRM-03` enforces the second.

### L1-802 — Framework rules: one active per role, non-retroactive, the marker literal

**PHASE:** L1.8 · **SIZE:** L · **DEPENDS:** L1-801 · **SPEC:** §77.1 ("Exactly one framework version is Active for a given role at a given date, unless multi-framework operation is explicitly configured for a transition period"); §77.4 (the marker literal); §84.2; AT-077; AT-078; SIG-23
**FILES:** `validators/registry/rules/r_frm_01.py`, `r_frm_02.py`, `r_frm_03.py`, `validators/registry/tests/test_framework_rules.py`, `validators/registry/fixtures/frm/**`

All three carry `APPLIES_TO = ["framework", "roles"]`.

| Id | `SPEC` | Condition | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R-FRM-01` | `Section 77.1` | for a role named in any `affected_roles`, the number of framework documents with `status: active` whose `[effective_date, retirement_date)` interval contains `ctx.today` is not exactly one, and no such document sets `multi_framework_transition: true` | `role '<r>' has <n> active frameworks on <date>; Section 77.1 permits exactly one unless multi_framework_transition is set; SIG-23` |
| `R-FRM-02` | `Section 77.4 / AT-078` | a framework's `effective_date` is earlier than the `retirement_date` of a document it supersedes for the same role | `framework <v> takes effect on <d1>, before <prev> retired on <d2>; AT-078 forbids a retroactive activation` |
| `R-FRM-03` | `Section 77.4 / AT-077` | a `target`, `stretch_target`, `definition` or `review_cadence` whose value is a **marker-shaped** string that is not exactly `Not defined in Framework v1` | `field '<f>' on '<id>' reads '<v>'; Section 77.4 requires the exact marker "Not defined in Framework v1" where the framework in force defines no value` |

**R-FRM-01 covers zero and two.** §77.1 says "exactly one", so both a role with none and a role with two fail. A role with none is SIG-23, "Outstanding framework mapping"; a role with two is the AT-077 failure. Both carry the same rule id and different `<n>` in the message.

**R-FRM-03's marker-shape set is closed and mechanical.** A value is marker-shaped when its casefolded, whitespace-collapsed form is one of: `not defined`, `not defined in framework v1`, `not defined in framework v1.`, `undefined`, `n/a`, `na`, `none`, `tbd`, `tba`, `to be defined`, `pending`, `unknown`. Any of those that is not **byte-identical** to `Not defined in Framework v1` is an error. §77.4: "Where a field genuinely does not exist in the framework in force, it is marked exactly: `Not defined in Framework v1`. **No value is invented to fill it.**" A near-miss marker is how a captured gap silently becomes a claim.

`review_cadence` is the one exception, and it is §77.1's, not yours: `review_cadence: "Not defined"` is a **valid** value there and R-FRM-03 must not fire on it. `valid/review_cadence_not_defined/` proves it. Everywhere else `Not defined` alone is an error.

### L1-803 — Banned-measurement and non-delegable-capability rules

**PHASE:** L1.8 · **SIZE:** L · **DEPENDS:** L1-802, L1-302 · **SPEC:** §91.2 (the eleven banned measurement classes); §90.4 (D109, not delegable); §74.5 (the authority matrix, D108); invariants 37, 96, 97, 98, 99, 106; AT-071; AT-075; AT-090
**FILES:** `validators/registry/rules/r_ban_01.py`, `validators/registry/rules/r_ban_02.py`, `validators/registry/rules/r_ban_03.py`, `validators/registry/tests/test_banned_rules.py`, `validators/registry/fixtures/ban/**`

Three denial rules. Each makes one prohibition mechanically unconfigurable, which is exactly what its acceptance test asks for.

| Id | `SPEC` | `APPLIES_TO` | Condition | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `R-BAN-01` | `Section 91.2` | `["framework", "os-health"]` | a `kpis[].id`, `kpis[].title`, `kpis[].definition`, `kpis[].evidence_sources[]`, `signals[].name`, `signals[].definition` or `signals[].source` whose normalised form contains a banned token | `banned measurement '<token>' appears at <pointer>; Section 91.2, invariants 96-99, AT-075` |
| `R-BAN-02` | `Section 90.4 (D109)` | `["product", "service", "people"]` | an assignment whose `scope.capabilities` contains `people-intelligence`, **or** a `founder_decision_delegate` whose `scope.decisions` names any of the ten §74.5 excluded decisions | `assignment '<type>' for '<p>' grants '<c>', which is not delegable; D109, invariant 106, AT-090` |
| `R-BAN-03` | `Section 91.2 / invariant 37` | `["framework", "os-health", "policies", "people", "product"]` | any **property name** anywhere in the document that is in the closed automated-people-action set | `field '<name>' at <pointer> configures an automated formal people action; invariant 37, AT-071` |

**The R-BAN-01 token set**, normalised (casefold, then every run of non-alphanumeric characters collapsed to a single `-`), derived from §91.2's eleven bullets plus invariants 96–99:

`keystroke`, `keylog`, `screen-monitoring`, `screenshot`, `screen-capture`, `activity-surveillance`, `webcam`, `presence-detection`, `hours-online`, `hours-at-desk`, `time-at-desk`, `token-usage`, `tokens-used`, `ide-active-time`, `active-editor-time`, `flight-risk`, `resignation-prediction`, `attrition-prediction`, `emotional-state`, `engagement-score`, `motivation-score`, `wellbeing-score`, `mental-health`, `surveillance-score`, `productivity-score`, `employee-ranking`, `leaderboard`, `stack-rank`

The match is **substring on the normalised form**, so `weekly-hours-online-report` hits `hours-online`.

**The R-BAN-03 property-name set**, closed: `auto_promote`, `auto_promotion`, `auto_terminate`, `auto_termination`, `auto_improvement_plan`, `auto_compensation_change`, `auto_formal_warning`, `automated_people_action`, `automatic_exit_decision`.

**The ten §74.5 excluded decisions** for R-BAN-02 are the same ten L1-302 already encoded for D108: `recognition`, `promotion`, `role-change-employment`, `hiring`, `formal-warning`, `improvement-plan`, `exit-consideration`, `compensation`, `permanent-headcount`, `people-intelligence`. ### L1-901 — Acceptance-test harness for the fourteen ATs Lane 1 can prove

**PHASE:** L1.9 · **SIZE:** L · **DEPENDS:** L1-803, L1-704 · **SPEC:** §100 (the acceptance-test catalogue); §100.1; §100.3; §100.4; §100.5; §99.2 subsystem B
**FILES:** `validators/registry/tests/test_acceptance.py`, `validators/registry/fixtures/acceptance/**`

An acceptance test is not a unit test. Each function here drives the **CLI**, from a fixture tree, and asserts the pass condition §100 states for that AT id — not the behaviour of a rule module.

**The fourteen, each with the Lane 1 evidence that proves it:**

| # | AT | §100 pass condition, in one line | Lane 1 evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `AT-001` | "No dashboard, workflow or script contains a product list" | no file under the four owned trees contains a hard-coded product-id list outside `fixtures/**` |
| 2 | `AT-007` | "Role profile plus performance-framework mapping added; no architecture change" | a twelfth role added to `roles.yaml` validates, and R-FRM-01 names it as unmapped, with zero schema edits |
| 3 | `AT-008` | "Scoped, dated, capability-limited entry … expiry handled" | a contractor with `scope`, a non-null `end_date` and a `temporary_contributor` assignment validates; the same record with `end_date: null` fails R-PPL-01 |
| 4 | `AT-009` | "The product conforms to the operating interface for its declared conformance profile" | one valid and one invalid fixture per profile through R-PRD-08 … R-PRD-25 |
| 5 | `AT-010` | "One product has three repositories … one contract, one owner set" | `code.repositories` with three entries validates; no `maxItems` exists |
| 6 | `AT-014` | "The new framework version activates; … No system rewrite" | a v2 framework with a different KPI count, different weights and a different rating scale validates against the same schema |
| 7 | `AT-016` | "Only `topology.yaml` changes; zero product contracts … are edited" | the byte-identical `product.yaml` pair from L1-503 |
| 8 | `AT-025` | "Both versions supported simultaneously" | the two-document single-run case from L1-701 |
| 9 | `AT-034` | "The delivery core runs correctly with the removable governance artifacts removed" | a tree with `os-health.yaml`, `policies.yaml`, `patterns.yaml`, `economics.yaml` and `platform-roadmap.yaml` deleted still validates clean |

**AT-034 is the sharpest of the fourteen** and it is worth stating why it belongs here. §100.3: "The reconciliation engine and the exception registry are core-resident machinery and are **never removed** — the core depends on them from day one." So `test_at034_governance_layerability` deletes the five named files and asserts the tree still validates, and it **also** asserts that deleting `registries/exceptions.yaml` from the same tree causes a failure. A test that only proved removability would have proved half the sentence.

**The fifteenth — now included.** `AT-047` — "a product declaring an extended or 24x7 support model whose declared `coverage_window` is not fully covered by the accepted windows of active rota members fails contract validation" — is provable by task **L1-311** (L1-D03 answered). Add `test_at047_coverage_window`; the count is now fifteen.

**A known count conflict, and how to handle it.** The Lane 1 charter's §9.2 lists **thirteen** provable ATs: AT-001, AT-007, AT-008, AT-009, AT-016, AT-025, AT-034, AT-047, AT-049, AT-051, AT-071, AT-075, AT-090. ### L1-902 — Invariant classification register and its CI rule

**PHASE:** L1.9 · **SIZE:** L · **DEPENDS:** L1-901, L1-604 · **SPEC:** §101 preamble (the enforcement-classification rule, in full); §55 (`policies.yaml` as the `policy` classification's carrier); §52.6; §0.7
**FILES:** `schemas/registry/invariants.v1.schema.json`, `registries/invariants.yaml`, `validators/registry/rules/r_inv_02.py`, `validators/registry/tests/test_invariant_classification.py`, `validators/registry/fixtures/invcls/**`

§101's preamble states the rule this task makes live, and it states the CI consequence itself:

> "Each of the 111 is exactly one of: **mechanical**, naming the CI check, branch-protection rule, reconciliation row or AT- identifier that enforces it; **policy**, naming the `policies.yaml` entry that carries its owner, review date and enforcement mechanism (Section 55); or **review-held**, naming the standing review that reads it and the role that chairs that review. … Control-plane CI fails when an invariant classified `mechanical` names no live check or AT- identifier, when one classified `policy` names no live `policies.yaml` entry, or when any invariant carries no classification at all."

**Schema shape** — top-level object, `additionalProperties: false`:

```
registry_version : {"const": 1}                                          required
declared_count   : integer, minimum 1                                    required
invariants : array (may be []), items addlProps false                    required
    number         : integer, minimum 1, maximum 111                     required
    text           : string minLength 1                                  required
    classification : enum [mechanical, policy, review-held]              required
    enforced_by    : string or null                                      required
    policy_id      : string or null                                      required
    review         : string or null                                      required
    chair          : string or null                                      required
```

**Rule `R-INV-02`** in `r_inv_02.py`. `SPEC = "Section 101 preamble"`, `APPLIES_TO = ["invariants", "policies"]`. Five limbs, four of them straight from the preamble:

| Limb | Condition | Message |
|---|---|---|
| a | `classification` absent or null | `invariant <n> carries no enforcement classification; Section 101` |
| b | `classification == mechanical` and `enforced_by` is null, or names neither a `RULE_ID` present in `RULES.md` nor a string matching `^AT-\d{3}$` | `invariant <n> is classified mechanical and names no live check or AT- identifier; Section 101` |
| c | `classification == policy` and `policy_id` names no `policies[].id` in the loaded `policies.yaml` | `invariant <n> is classified policy and names no live policies.yaml entry; Section 101` |
| d | `classification == review-held` and `review` or `chair` is null | `invariant <n> is classified review-held and names no standing review or chairing role; Section 101` |
| e | `invariants` is non-empty and `len(invariants) != declared_count` | `the invariant register holds <n> entries; declared_count is <m>; Section 101 states 111` |

**Limb e applies only to a non-empty register.** A file shipping `invariants: []` is an *unpopulated* register, not a *miscounted* one, and firing on it every run would make the rule noise from day one. State this in the module docstring.

Limb c returns zero errors when `policies.yaml` is absent from `ctx.docs`, exactly as R-PPL-04 does.

**`registries/invariants.yaml` ships with `invariants: []` and `declared_count: 111`.** Classifying all 111 requires naming the live check for each, and most of those checks belong to **Lane 2** (workflow and branch-protection contexts), **Lane 3** (reconciliation rows) and **Lane 5** (access enforcement). PARTITION rule 4 forbids Lane 1 reaching into their trees to discover check names, and rule 2 routes cross-lane consumption through `contracts/**`. Lane 1 ships the register, the schema and the rule; the classifications land as each lane publishes its check ids. §98.5 Phase G2 is where the mapping is "authored … alongside the policy register it resolves into".

**STOP — this stop is unconditional; it fires every time.** §101's preamble says the classification mapping "needs no **twenty-seventh** control-plane artifact — `policies.yaml` already holds owners and review dates, so what is new is the mapping, not a register." Three things follow, and none is yours to resolve:

1. §101 says **twenty-seven**; §52.6 says **twenty-nine**; §52.6's table renders **thirty**. Three counts, three places.
2. §101 says the mapping is "not a register", and this task ships `registries/invariants.yaml`, which is a register. The master table names that file, so the task ships it.
3. §0.7 of this document forbids a thirtieth control-plane artifact under `registries/**`, and this is the third such file after `OWNERS.yaml` and `INVENTORY.yaml`.

The L1-505 blocker already carries limbs 2 and 3 for all three files. **Add a comment to that issue rather than opening a duplicate**, and open a new blocker only for limb 1, which L1-505 does not cover:

* Title: `BLOCKER L1 L1-902: Section 101 says twenty-seven control-plane artifacts, Section 52.6 says twenty-nine, and its table renders thirty`
* Body must contain, verbatim: §101's "needs no twenty-seventh control-plane artifact" sentence; §52.6's "twenty-nine entries" sentence; the `ARTIFACTS=30` output from L1-505's self-verify; and a pointer to the L1-505 issue number.
* `DECIDER: L0 Integrator` · `BLOCKS: L1-704's R-INV-01 stays known-red until this is answered`

### L1-903 — Publish the stable CLI interface Lane 2 wires into CI

**PHASE:** L1.9 · **SIZE:** M · **DEPENDS:** L1-902 · **SPEC:** §99.2 subsystem B; PARTITION rule 2 (cross-lane consumption routes through a published artifact) and rule 4 (never by reaching into a source tree); L1-003's frozen grammar
**FILES:** `validators/registry/README.md`, `validators/registry/tests/test_readme_contract.py`

Lane 2 owns `.github/workflows/**` and consumes Lane 1's output. PARTITION rule 4: "A lane consumes another lane's output only through `contracts/**` or a published artifact — never by reaching into its source tree." This README **is** that published artifact, and the frozen grammar of L1-003 is what it publishes.

**`validators/registry/README.md` contains exactly these five sections and nothing else:**

1. **Invocation** — the one command line Lane 2 calls, verbatim from L1-003's frozen grammar:
   `python -m validators.registry.cli --root <p> --as-of <d> --records-root <p> --format json [--rule Rxx]`  # FD-094: Option B grammar — updated 2026-09-09
2. **Exit codes** — 0=pass, 1=fail, 2=input error.
3. **Output grammar** — JSON on stdout; the error line `ERROR <RULE-ID> <path>:<json-pointer> <message>`; exit 2 on bad flags or unreadable paths.
4. **Determinism** — `--today` overrides "now" for every date rule; absent, it uses the system UTC date. Every CI invocation must pass `--today` explicitly so a run is reproducible.
5. **Stability** — the grammar is frozen from L1-003 onward. Changing it is a Contract Change Request under PARTITION rule 2, not an edit. Lane 2 keys its required status check on the exit code, never on parsing prose.

**The README documents no path outside the four owned trees**, names no workflow file, and prescribes no CI configuration. Lane 2 decides how to invoke it; Lane 1 decides only what it does.

`validators/registry/tests/test_readme_contract.py` holds exactly six functions:

| Test | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `test_documents_all_four_exit_codes` | the README names 0, 1, 2 and 3 with the L1-003 meanings |
| `test_success_line_matches_report_module` | the documented success line equals `report.render_text([], 1)` |
| `test_failure_line_matches_report_module` | the documented failure line format equals what `report.render_text` emits for one error |
| `test_lists_every_flag_of_the_frozen_grammar` | every flag `cli.main` accepts appears in the README |
| `test_claims_no_flag_the_cli_lacks` | every flag the README names is accepted by `cli.main` |
| `test_names_no_path_outside_the_owned_trees` | no path string in the README begins with anything other than `schemas/registry/`, `schemas/product/`, `registries/` or `validators/registry/` |

Tests 4 and 5 are deliberately a pair. One catches a README that has fallen behind the CLI; the other catches a README that promises a flag the CLI never had. Either failure mode silently breaks Lane 2's workflow, and only one of them is caught by running the CLI.

```bash
python -m validators.registry.cli --help
python -c "from validators.registry.report import render_text; print(render_text([], 1))"
```

### L1-904 — Full-lane regression and runtime budget

**PHASE:** L1.9 · **SIZE:** M · **DEPENDS:** L1-903 · **SPEC:** §99.2 subsystem B; §0.7; PARTITION rules 1 and 3; AT-102's principle ("a validator that finds nothing is assumed broken")
**FILES:** `validators/registry/tools/lane_verify.sh`

One script, `set -euo pipefail`, run from `$REPO_ROOT`. It proves six things and prints `LANE 1 VERIFY OK` only when all six hold.

**Invocation:**

```
bash validators/registry/tools/lane_verify.sh [--with-l1-311 | --without-l1-311]
```

`--without-l1-311` was the default while L1-D03 was open; L1-D03 is now resolved (2026-09-16) and L1-311 is unblocked.

**The six checks:**

| # | Check | How |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The whole suite passes at the expected count | `python -m pytest validators/registry/tests -q`, then assert the summary line is exactly `698 passed, 3 xfailed` without `--with-l1-311`, or `708 passed, 3 xfailed` with it |
| 2 | Every rule module is discoverable and well-formed | `discover()` returns without raising, and every returned module exposes all four names |
| 3 | Every discovered rule has a row in `RULES.md`, and every `R-` row in `RULES.md` is discoverable | set equality both ways |
| 4 | Every live registry file validates, or fails only for a recorded known-red reason | run the CLI over `registries/` with `--today`, and assert the error set equals exactly the two known-red errors: R-CAP-02 on the `founder` row (L1-103) and R-INV-01 on the artifact count (L1-505) |
| 5 | No file outside the four owned trees was touched by this lane | `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` matches only `schemas/registry/`, `schemas/product/`, `registries/`, `validators/registry/` |
| 6 | The suite runs inside the runtime budget | wall-clock under 120 seconds |

**The three xfails are named, not counted loosely.** They are: the `spec_founder_row` case at L1-202, and the two conformance clauses at L1-308 (`R-PRD-21`'s consumer-contract clause and `R-PRD-23`'s exception-resolution clause). The script asserts the pytest summary names exactly `3 xfailed`; a fourth xfail means a test was silenced rather than fixed, and that is a failure of check 1.

**Check 4 is the AT-102 principle applied to this lane.** A lane_verify that reported "no errors" over a live tree carrying two known contradictions would be a validator that found nothing, and §53.1's seeded-canary discipline says such a run is assumed broken. The two known-red errors are the lane's own canary: if either stops firing, either L0 answered a blocker — in which case the script's expected set changes in the same commit as the fix — or a rule silently stopped working.

**The runtime budget is a Lane 1 declaration, not a spec citation.** §51.2's platform SLOs are **Lane 5**'s and govern the control plane's services, not this suite. 120 seconds is chosen so the gate stays usable as a pre-push check. If the suite exceeds it, that is a STOP.

Two of these leave the live tree **known-red by design** — L1-103's R-CAP-02 on `registries/roles.yaml` and L1-505's R-INV-01 on `registries/OWNERS.yaml`. Both are asserted by name in `lane_verify.sh` check 4. **Neither is a defect to be fixed inside this lane, and neither may be silenced by editing a registry file.** They are the lane's canary: while they fire, the validator is demonstrably discriminating; if either stops firing without an L0 answer in the same commit, task L1-904's STOP rule applies.

### L1-908 — L1-00-03 — Install the lane self-guard <!-- canonical ID: L1-0NN per FD-031 Two-part grammar -->

<!-- absorbed from L1-00-03 per FD-095, 2026-09-09 -->

**Size:** S **Depends on:** L1-00-02 <!-- canonical ID: L1-0NN per FD-031 Two-part grammar -->

**Creates:** `validators/registry/_meta/lane_paths.sh`

This script is run by **every** later L1 task before committing. It is the lane's own copy of PARTITION rule 1.

**Commands**

```bash
set -e
cat > validators/registry/_meta/lane_paths.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lane 1 self-guard. Fails if the working tree or the branch diff touches a foreign path.
# PARTITION.md rule 1: "One owner per path. A lane PR touching a foreign path FAILS."
# Owned prefixes are copied verbatim from PARTITION.md line 17 and are not editable here.
set -euo pipefail
ALLOW='^(schemas/registry/|schemas/product/|registries/|validators/registry/)'
BASE="${1:-integration}"

changed="$( { git diff --name-only "$BASE"...HEAD 2>/dev/null || true;
              git status --porcelain | awk '{print $2}'; } | sort -u )"

bad="$(printf '%s\n' "$changed" | grep -v -E "$ALLOW" | grep -v '^$' || true)"

if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
  echo "LANE-GUARD-FAIL: foreign paths touched by lane/1:"
  printf '%s\n' "$bad"
  exit 1
fi
echo "LANE-GUARD-PASS"
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x validators/registry/_meta/lane_paths.sh
./validators/registry/_meta/lane_paths.sh integration
echo "T03-PASS"
```

**Acceptance criteria**

| # | Criterion | Proving command | Unambiguous correct output |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | The guard exists and is executable | `test -x validators/registry/_meta/lane_paths.sh; echo $?` | `0` |
| A2 | The guard passes on the current clean lane branch | `./validators/registry/_meta/lane_paths.sh integration` | `LANE-GUARD-PASS` |
| A3 | The guard actually catches a foreign path | `touch docs/__probe.tmp && ./validators/registry/_meta/lane_paths.sh integration; echo "exit=$?"; rm -f docs/__probe.tmp` | first line `LANE-GUARD-FAIL: foreign paths touched by lane/1:`, last line `exit=1` |

**SELF-VERIFY**

```bash
set -euo pipefail
./validators/registry/_meta/lane_paths.sh integration && echo "T03-VERIFIED"
```

Correct output: `LANE-GUARD-PASS` then `T03-VERIFIED`.

**STOP rule** — do not proceed if A3 does **not** produce `exit=1`. A guard that fails to catch a deliberately planted foreign path is a broken guard, and every later L1 task depends on it. Delete `docs/__probe.tmp` if it survives, then file the blocker of §13 with `BLOCKER-KIND: GUARD-BROKEN`.

Every later L1 document cites spec sections by line range. If the spec file changes, those citations rot silently.
This task pins them and gives the lane a one-command drift check.

**Commands**

```bash
set -e
SPEC="C:/D_Drive/PS/MultiProduct/Research/MultiProduct_MasterSpec_v4.0.md"
test -f "$SPEC" || { echo "FAIL: spec not found at $SPEC"; exit 1; }

cat > validators/registry/_meta/spec-anchors.tsv <<'EOF'
# heading_regex	expected_start_line	charter_section_id
^## Section 7\. People Registry	543	7
^## Section 8\. Role Registry	634	8
^## Section 9\. Capability Model	687	9
^## Section 10\. Assignment Registry and Delegation	725	10
^## Section 15\. Product Operating Contract	1284	15
^## Section 20\. Shared Services and the Dependency Graph	2027	20
^## Section 21\. Customer Commitments and SLA Registry	2113	21
^### 26\.4 The registry-change lane	2526	26.4
^## Section 31\. Verification Contract	2741	31
^### 38\.1 The ai_runtime_dependency block	3373	38.1
^### 44\.1 Per-product declarations	3963	44.1
^### 52\.6 Registry of control-plane files	4613	52.6
^## Section 54\. Exception Registry and Break-Glass	4746	54
^## Section 55\. Policy Lifecycle and Gradual Enforcement	4830	55
^## Section 60\. Platform Versioning, Versioned Contracts and Compatibility	5119	60
^### 62\.1 The tool register	5289	62.1
^### 64\.1 Safe defaults	5433	64.1
^### 66\.2 Domains	5508	66.2
^### 68\.1 The Product Load Unit	5624	68.1
^## Section 77\. Performance Framework Registry	6339	77
^### 91\.2 No-surveillance design	8079	91.2
^### 96\.2 Pre-onboarding operating mode	8720	96.2
^### 99\.2 The subsystem architecture	9184	99.2
^## Section 100\. Acceptance Tests	9295	100
^## Section 101\. Non-Negotiable Invariants	9443	101
EOF

cat > validators/registry/_meta/check_spec_anchors.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verifies every spec line-range citation used by Lane 1 still resolves.
# Usage: check_spec_anchors.sh <path-to-MultiProduct_MasterSpec_v4.0.md>
set -euo pipefail
SPEC="${1:?usage: check_spec_anchors.sh <spec-file>}"
TSV="$(dirname "$0")/spec-anchors.tsv"
fail=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r re want id; do
  case "$re" in \#*|'') continue;; esac
  got="$(grep -n -m1 -E "$re" "$SPEC" | cut -d: -f1)"
  if [ "$got" != "$want" ]; then
    echo "ANCHOR-DRIFT: section $id expected line $want, found '${got:-none}'"
    fail=1
  fi
done < "$TSV"
if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then echo "SPEC-ANCHORS-FAIL"; exit 1; fi
echo "SPEC-ANCHORS-PASS"
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x validators/registry/_meta/check_spec_anchors.sh
./validators/registry/_meta/check_spec_anchors.sh "$SPEC"
echo "T04-PASS"
```

| A2 | Every anchor resolves | `./validators/registry/_meta/check_spec_anchors.sh "C:/D_Drive/PS/MultiProduct/Research/MultiProduct_MasterSpec_v4.0.md"` | `SPEC-ANCHORS-PASS` |
| A3 | The lane guard still passes | `./validators/registry/_meta/lane_paths.sh integration` | `LANE-GUARD-PASS` |

```bash
./validators/registry/_meta/check_spec_anchors.sh "C:/D_Drive/PS/MultiProduct/Research/MultiProduct_MasterSpec_v4.0.md" \
  && ./validators/registry/_meta/lane_paths.sh integration \
  && echo "T04-VERIFIED"
```

**STOP rule** — do not proceed if any line prints `ANCHOR-DRIFT`. The spec has moved under this charter, and every
line-range citation in every L1 document is now suspect. **Do not "fix" the numbers.** File the blocker of §13 with
`BLOCKER-KIND: SPEC-DRIFT`, listing every `ANCHOR-DRIFT` line verbatim, and stop.

### L1-912 — L1-01-02 — Repository bootstrap: `git init`, `gh repo create`, initial commit <!-- canonical ID: L1-0NN per FD-031 Two-part grammar -->

<!-- absorbed from L1-01-02 per FD-095, 2026-09-09 -->

**Size:** S **Depends on:** T01
**Creates/edits:** the `control-plane` repository object; `registries/.gitkeep` (owned path) as the sole file of the initial commit.

**Why the initial commit contains only `registries/.gitkeep`.** A git commit must contain at least one file. `README.md` and `.gitignore` are root files and belong to L0 (PARTITION.md, L0 row). `registries/.gitkeep` is inside an L1-owned path, so the bootstrap commit violates no ownership rule. L0 adds the root files in its own commit; the handover text is prepared by T12.

### Commands

```bash
set -euo pipefail
export CP_REPO="control-plane"
export CP_ROOT="/c/D_Drive/PS/MultiProduct/control-plane"

# --- Step 1: is the repository already created (e.g. by L0 Phase 0)? ---
if gh repo view "$CP_ORG/$CP_REPO" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "REPO_EXISTS"
else
  echo "REPO_ABSENT"
fi
```

**Branch A — output was `REPO_ABSENT`. Run the full bootstrap:**

```bash
set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p "$CP_ROOT"
cd "$CP_ROOT"

git init --initial-branch=main
git config user.name  "$(gh api user --jq .login)"
git config user.email "$(gh api user --jq '.email // "noreply@users.noreply.github.com"')"

mkdir -p registries
: > registries/.gitkeep

git add registries/.gitkeep
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
chore(l1): bootstrap control-plane repository

Creates the control-plane repository required by spec Section 98.2
Phase 1 ("Create the control-plane repository") and Section 99.2
subsystem A.

The commit carries only registries/.gitkeep because every root file
(README.md, .gitignore, Makefile, CODEOWNERS) is owned by L0 under the
frozen partition contract; L1 owns registries/** and adds nothing else
here.

Refs: spec Sections 98.2, 99.2 (subsystem A), 52.6
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

gh repo create "$CP_ORG/$CP_REPO" \
  --private \
  --source . \
  --remote origin \
  --description "Control plane: registries, contracts, schemas, validators (spec Section 99.2 subsystem A)" \
  --push

git branch integration main
git push -u origin integration
```

**Branch B — output was `REPO_EXISTS`. Clone instead of creating:**

```bash
set -euo pipefail
rm -rf "$CP_ROOT"
gh repo clone "$CP_ORG/$CP_REPO" "$CP_ROOT"
cd "$CP_ROOT"
git fetch origin
git checkout integration 2>/dev/null || { git checkout -b integration origin/main && git push -u origin integration; }
mkdir -p registries && : > registries/.gitkeep
git add registries/.gitkeep
git diff --cached --quiet || git commit -m "chore(l1): add registries/ root for lane 1

Refs: spec Sections 98.2, 99.2 (subsystem A)
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
git push origin integration
```

### Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Proving command | Unambiguous expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Repository exists on GitHub | `gh repo view "$CP_ORG/$CP_REPO" --json name --jq .name` | `control-plane` |
| 2 | Repository is private | `gh repo view "$CP_ORG/$CP_REPO" --json isPrivate --jq .isPrivate` | `true` |
| 3 | Local clone is a git work tree | `cd "$CP_ROOT" && git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` | `true` |
| 4 | `origin` points at the right repo | `cd "$CP_ROOT" && git remote get-url origin \| grep -c "$CP_REPO"` | `1` |
| 5 | `main` exists on the remote | `gh api "repos/$CP_ORG/$CP_REPO/branches/main" --jq .name` | `main` |
| 6 | `integration` exists on the remote | `gh api "repos/$CP_ORG/$CP_REPO/branches/integration" --jq .name` | `integration` |
| 7 | No foreign path in history | `cd "$CP_ROOT" && git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD \| grep -vcE '^(schemas/registry/|schemas/product/|registries/|validators/registry/)'` | `0` |

Criterion 7 is the ownership proof. If it returns anything other than `0` on Branch A, the bootstrap wrote a file it must not have; delete that file and re-commit before proceeding. On Branch B a non-zero count is expected only for files L0 already committed — in that case run instead:

```bash
cd "$CP_ROOT"
git log --format=%H -n1 -- . >/dev/null
git show --stat --name-only --format="" HEAD | grep -vcE '^(schemas/registry/|schemas/product/|registries/|validators/registry/)|^$'
```
which must print `0` (this lane's own last commit touched owned paths only).

### SELF-VERIFY

```bash
cd "$CP_ROOT"
A=$(gh repo view "$CP_ORG/$CP_REPO" --json name --jq .name)
B=$(gh repo view "$CP_ORG/$CP_REPO" --json isPrivate --jq .isPrivate)
C=$(git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree)
D=$(gh api "repos/$CP_ORG/$CP_REPO/branches/integration" --jq .name 2>/dev/null)
E=$(git show --stat --name-only --format="" HEAD | grep -vcE '^(schemas/registry/|schemas/product/|registries/|validators/registry/)|^$')
if [ "$A" = "control-plane" ] && [ "$B" = "true" ] && [ "$C" = "true" ] \
   && [ "$D" = "integration" ] && [ "$E" = "0" ]; then echo "T02 PASS"; else echo "T02 FAIL A=$A B=$B C=$C D=$D E=$E"; fi
```

**Correct output:** the single line `T02 PASS`.

### STOP rule

Do not proceed if `gh repo create` fails with `HTTP 403`, `Resource not accessible by integration`, or `Name already exists on this account` in a form Branch B cannot handle. Do not create the repository under your personal account as a substitute. Do not make it public.

File the §0.6 blocker with `<TASKID>` = `T02` and `<BLOCKED_ON key>` = one of `no-org-repo-create-permission`, `org-login-wrong`, `repo-name-collision`.

> **DECISION REQUIRED — L0**
> **Subject:** GitHub organisation login and repository visibility for `control-plane`.
> **Why L1 cannot decide it:** the organisation login is estate configuration, not a lane artifact; §98.2 Phase 1 requires "one company-owned GitHub organisation" but names no login, and §99.5 fixes only the host (GitHub) and the plan tier (Team, D73).
> **What L0 must supply, exactly:** the value of `CP_ORG`, in the T02 task issue, before T02 is dispatched.
> **Blocking:** T02 and everything after it.

### L1-914 — L1-01-04 — Per-directory `.gitignore` files inside owned paths <!-- canonical ID: L1-0NN per FD-031 Two-part grammar -->

<!-- absorbed from L1-01-04 per FD-095, 2026-09-09 -->

**Size:** S **Depends on:** T03
**Creates/edits:**
```
registries/.gitignore
schemas/registry/.gitignore
schemas/product/.gitignore
validators/registry/.gitignore
```

**Why not a root `.gitignore`.** The root `.gitignore` is an L0-owned root file (PARTITION.md, L0 row). Git honours a `.gitignore` in any directory, so this lane's ignore rules live in its own directories and require no foreign write. The proposed **root** `.gitignore` text is handed to L0 by T12.

### Commands

```bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$CP_ROOT"

cat > registries/.gitignore <<'EOF'
# Lane 1 (Registries & Contracts) — registries/ ignore rules.
# Owned by L1 per the frozen partition contract. The ROOT .gitignore is
# owned by L0; see validators/registry/l0-handover/root-gitignore.proposed.
#
# Registries are the declared source of truth (spec Section 5.1) and are
# append-only under effective dating (Sections 63.1, 101.7 #47). Nothing
# generated, derived or transient may be committed beside them, because a
# derived file beside a declared one is how "derived data is computed,
# never hand-maintained" (invariant 46) silently stops being true.

*.generated.yaml
*.generated.yml
*.derived.yaml
*.derived.yml
*.rendered.yaml
*.bak
*.orig
*.rej
*~
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db
EOF

cat > schemas/registry/.gitignore <<'EOF'
# Lane 1 (Registries & Contracts) — schemas/registry/ ignore rules.
# schemas/registry/** is exclusively owned by L1 (PARTITION.md rule 1).
# Compiled or bundled schema output is build product, never source.

*.bundle.json
*.compiled.json
*.resolved.json
node_modules/
__pycache__/
*.pyc
*.bak
*.orig
*.rej
*~
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db
EOF

cat > schemas/product/.gitignore <<'EOF'
# Lane 1 (Registries & Contracts) — schemas/product/ ignore rules.
# schemas/product/** is exclusively owned by L1 (PARTITION.md rule 1).
# Compiled or bundled schema output is build product, never source.

*.bundle.json
*.compiled.json
*.resolved.json
node_modules/
__pycache__/
*.pyc
*.bak
*.orig
*.rej
*~
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db
EOF

cat > validators/registry/.gitignore <<'EOF'
# Lane 1 (Registries & Contracts) — validators/registry/ ignore rules.
# Validator run output is evidence, and evidence lives in the records
# repository (Section 97.1, D89), never here.

.venv/
__pycache__/
*.pyc
*.log
report/
out/
*.bak
*.orig
*.rej
*~
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db
EOF

git add registries/.gitignore schemas/registry/.gitignore schemas/product/.gitignore validators/registry/.gitignore
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
chore(l1): per-directory .gitignore for lane-1 owned paths

Ignore rules live in the lane's own directories because the root
.gitignore is an L0-owned root file under the frozen partition contract.
Excludes generated, derived and transient files from the declared-state
paths, per invariant 46 (derived data is computed, never hand-maintained)
and Section 97.1/D89 (validator output is evidence and belongs in the
records repository).

Refs: spec Sections 5.1, 97.1, 101.7 #46
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
git push origin lane/1/01-repo-skeleton
```

| 2 | No root `.gitignore` created by this lane | `git ls-files \| grep -c '^\.gitignore$'` | `0` |
| 3 | No bare `schemas/.gitignore` (foreign path) | `git ls-files \| grep -c '^schemas/\.gitignore$'` | `0` |
| 4 | All tracked gitignores are inside owned prefixes | `git ls-files \| grep '\.gitignore$' \| grep -vcE '^(schemas/registry/|schemas/product/|registries/|validators/registry/)'` | `0` |

### L1-915 — L1-01-05 — `schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md`: effective dating and append-only <!-- canonical ID: L1-0NN per FD-031 Two-part grammar -->

<!-- absorbed from L1-01-05 per FD-095, 2026-09-09 -->

**Size:** M **Depends on:** T03
**Creates/edits:** `schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md`

This is the day-one discipline §99.4 item 1 says cannot be retrofitted. Every rule below is transcribed from a cited spec line; none is invented.

### Commands

```bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$CP_ROOT"
cat > schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md <<'EOF'
# Registry record conventions — effective dating and append-only

**Status:** binding from the first commit of this repository.
**Owner:** Lane 1 (Registries & Contracts), subsystems A and B of spec Section 99.2.
**Scope:** every file under `registries/**`, and every schema under
`schemas/registry/**` and `schemas/product/**` that validates one.

## 0. Why this file exists before anything else

Spec Section 99.4, item 1 of the minimal honest V1:

> Control-plane repository, schemas and CI validation — with effective dating and
> append-only discipline from the start, because retrofitting history is impossible
> by definition.

Spec Section 63.1 marks immutable history **Priority: P0 — retrofitting history is
impossible by definition**, and invariant 47 (Section 101.7) makes it
non-negotiable:

> History is append-only for state, decisions, approvals and records; records are
> not deleted and state changes are recorded, not overwritten.

## 1. The effective-dating mechanism

Section 63.1 states the mechanism exactly:

> **Mechanism:** state transitions with `start_date` and `end_date` — effective-dating,
> never in-place mutation — plus git history in the control-plane repository as the
> durable record. No separate audit database is introduced.

Therefore:

* **C1 — Dated fields are named `start_date` and `end_date`.** No synonym is
  permitted anywhere in `registries/**`: not `from`/`to`, not `valid_from`,
  not `effective_from`, not `since`. Section 7 uses `start_date` and `end_date`
  on every person record; Section 60.3 uses `deadline` for a migration target,
  which is a different concept and is not an effective-dating field.
* **C2 — `end_date` is always present, and `null` means open-ended.** An absent
  key is a malformed record, not an open interval. Section 7 writes
  `end_date: null` explicitly on an open-ended employee record.
* **C3 — `end_date` is mandatory and non-null for every non-employee.**
  Section 7.1: "`end_date` **is mandatory for every non-employee.** A CI check
  fails if a contractor, intern, temporary specialist or consultant has a null
  end date."
* **C4 — Dates are ISO-8601 calendar dates, `YYYY-MM-DD`.** Timestamps, where a
  registry carries one, are UTC with offset, per Section 97.1: "Every record and
  event timestamp is stored in UTC with its offset."
* **C5 — Business-day and working-hour rules never resolve against a runner's
  local clock.** Section 97.1: they resolve "against the declared working
  calendar and operating timezone held in the leave records (Section 6.4) —
  never against a runner's local time." Timezones in `registries/people.yaml`
  are IANA identifiers, never UTC offsets (Section 7 `work_arrangement.timezone`).

## 2. The append-only rules

Section 63.1 names what is never overwritten destructively:

> ownership, reviewer assignments, platform versions in use, product lifecycle
> state, assignments, approvals, policy text, exception records, classification
> and both criticality fields, domain membership.

Therefore:

* **A1 — Identifiers are stable and are never reused.** Section 63.1: "The system
  refuses to delete departed people and refuses to reuse identifiers." Section 7
  marks the person `id` "stable identifier, never reused". A validator enforces
  this; see `validators/registry/check-append-only.sh`.
* **A2 — A state change closes the old interval and opens a new one.** Set the
  old entry's `end_date`; add a new entry. Never edit a field of a closed
  interval in place.
* **A3 — Departure is a state, not a deletion.** Section 7.1: "A departed
  person's record is retained with `availability: departed` and
  `access_status: revoked` so that historical evidence — who approved what, who
  reviewed what — remains interpretable. Their identifier is never reused."
* **A4 — Corrections are follow-up entries, never in-place rewrites.** Section
  97.2 states this for records — "never edits in place (corrections are
  follow-up records)" — and Section 63.1 generalises the principle to "every
  operating-system record".
* **A5 — Git history is the audit trail.** No separate audit file, no changelog
  registry, no "history" block inside a registry file. Section 63.1 is explicit
  that git plus GitHub's audit log plus the deployment records already carry it.
* **A6 — No shared mutable index.** One entry per item; period and portfolio
  views are derived by aggregation, never by appending to a shared list file.
  Section 97.3 states the rule for events — "written as its own file, one file
  per event, never a concurrent append to a shared period file" — and it is why
  parallel work in this repository never contends for the same file.

## 3. Version fields

Section 60.2 fixes the version field per contract. The three this lane seeds in
Phase 1:

| Contract | File | Version field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| People Registry | `registries/people.yaml` | `registry_version` |
| Role Registry | `registries/roles.yaml` | `registry_version` |
| Event-type enum and platform record | `registries/platform.yaml` | `platform_version` |

* **V1 — A schema change writes v2 alongside v1; it never replaces v1.**
  Section 60.2: "Write the v2 schema alongside v1 — do not replace"; the
  validator supports both; v1 support is removed only after every consumer has
  migrated.
* **V2 — Simultaneous fleet migration is never required** (Section 60.2).

## 4. The telemetry carve-out

Section 63.1 and Section 97.6: append-only permanence applies to state,
decisions, approvals and records. Raw activity telemetry may be aggregated or
discarded after its declared diagnostic window, and retention classes are
declared in the control plane and owned by the Founder. Nothing in
`registries/**` is telemetry, so the carve-out never applies to a file this lane
owns.

## 5. What this file does NOT govern

* `records/**` and `events/**` live in the **`control-plane-records`** repository,
  not here (Section 52.6 row for `records/`/`events/`; Section 40.1, D89). Their
  envelopes carry `record_schema_version` and `event_schema_version`
  (Section 97.2, 97.3) and are owned by Lane 4.
* Layer B stores and the conduct-records store are never in any org-readable
  repository (Section 52.6, Section 90).
EOF

git add schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
docs(l1): registry effective-dating and append-only conventions

The day-one discipline of Section 99.4 item 1 — effective dating and
append-only from the start, because retrofitting history is impossible
by definition. Mechanism transcribed from Section 63.1 (start_date /
end_date, git as the durable record), rules from Sections 7.1, 60.2,
97.1, 97.2, 97.3, 97.6 and invariant 101.7 #47.

Refs: spec Sections 7.1, 60.2, 63.1, 97, 99.4, 101.7 #47
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
git push origin lane/1/01-repo-skeleton
```

### Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Proving command | Unambiguous expected output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | File exists and is tracked | `git ls-files schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md` | `schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md` |
| 2 | All six append-only rules present | `grep -c '^\* \*\*A[1-6] ' schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md` | `6` |
| 3 | All five dating rules present | `grep -c '^\* \*\*C[1-5] ' schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md` | `5` |
| 4 | Both version rules present | `grep -c '^\* \*\*V[1-2] ' schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md` | `2` |
| 5 | No forbidden date synonym is used as a field | `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*(valid_from|effective_from|since):' schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md` | `0` |
| 6 | Section 99.4 quote present verbatim | `grep -c 'retrofitting history is impossible' schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md` | `3` |
| 7 | Records/events correctly disclaimed | `grep -c 'control-plane-records' schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md` | `1` |

### SELF-VERIFY

```bash
cd "$CP_ROOT"
A=$(grep -c '^\* \*\*A[1-6] ' schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md)
C=$(grep -c '^\* \*\*C[1-5] ' schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md)
V=$(grep -c '^\* \*\*V[1-2] ' schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md)
R=$(grep -c 'control-plane-records' schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md)
[ "$A" = "6" ] && [ "$C" = "5" ] && [ "$V" = "2" ] && [ "$R" = "1" ] \
  && echo "T05 PASS" || echo "T05 FAIL A=$A C=$C V=$V R=$R"
```

**Correct output:** the single line `T05 PASS`.

### STOP rule

Do not add, remove, reword or reorder any rule in this file. Every rule is a transcription of a cited spec line; changing one is a spec change, and a spec change is a Contract Change Request to L0 (PARTITION.md rule 2), never a lane edit. If a rule appears to contradict another lane's artifact, file the §0.6 blocker with `<TASKID>` = `T05`, `<BLOCKED_ON key>` = `convention-conflicts-with-contract`, quoting both texts.

### L1-916 — L1-01-06 — Shared effective-dating and envelope JSON Schemas <!-- canonical ID: L1-0NN per FD-031 Two-part grammar -->

<!-- absorbed from L1-01-06 per FD-095, 2026-09-09 -->


**Size:** M **Depends on:** T05
**Creates/edits:**
```
schemas/registry/common/effective-dating.schema.json
schemas/registry/common/registry-envelope.schema.json
```

### Commands

```bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$CP_ROOT"

cat > schemas/registry/common/effective-dating.schema.json <<'EOF'
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "x-needs-urn": "FD-050: replace with urn:multiproduct:schemas:<type>:<version>",
  "$id": "https://control-plane.invalid/schemas/registry/common/effective-dating.schema.json",
  "title": "Effective-dating primitives",
  "description": "Shared $defs for every control-plane registry. Mechanism per spec Section 63.1: state transitions with start_date and end_date, effective-dating, never in-place mutation. Rules C1-C5 and A1-A6 of schemas/registry/CONVENTIONS.md.",
  "$defs": {
    "date": {
      "title": "ISO-8601 calendar date",
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])$"
    },
    "utcTimestamp": {
      "title": "UTC timestamp with explicit offset (Section 97.1)",
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])T([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]:[0-5][0-9](\\.[0-9]+)?(Z|[+-]([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9])$"
    },
    "stableId": {
      "title": "Stable identifier, never reused (Sections 7, 63.1; rule A1)",
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$",
      "minLength": 2,
      "maxLength": 64
    },
    "ianaTimezone": {
      "title": "IANA timezone identifier, never a UTC offset (Section 7.3; rule C5)",
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_+-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_+-]+)+$"
    },
    "effectiveInterval": {
      "title": "An effective-dated interval",
      "description": "end_date is always present; null means open-ended (rule C2). Non-employees must carry a non-null end_date (rule C3, Section 7.1).",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "start_date": { "$ref": "#/$defs/date" },
        "end_date": {
          "anyOf": [
            { "$ref": "#/$defs/date" },
            { "type": "null" }
          ]
        }
      },
      "required": ["start_date", "end_date"]
    }
  }
}
EOF

cat > schemas/registry/common/registry-envelope.schema.json <<'EOF'
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "x-needs-urn": "FD-050: replace with urn:multiproduct:schemas:<type>:<version>",
  "$id": "https://control-plane.invalid/schemas/registry/common/registry-envelope.schema.json",
  "title": "Control-plane registry envelopes",
  "description": "Version-field envelopes per spec Section 60.2. People Registry and Role Registry carry registry_version; platform.yaml carries platform_version.",
  "$defs": {
    "registryEnvelope": {
      "title": "registry_version envelope (Section 60.2)",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "registry_version": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 }
      },
      "required": ["registry_version"]
    },
    "platformEnvelope": {
      "title": "platform_version envelope (Sections 60.1, 60.2)",
```
